chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said: O' groups of people, fear Allāh,
for there is many a man who aspires for what he does not get, many a builder of a house who does not live in it, and many a collector of that which he shall just leave behind.
Possibly he may have collected it wrongfully or by denying a right. He acquired it unlawfully and had to bear the weight of sins on account of it.
Consequently, he returned (from this world) with that weight and came before Allāh with sorrow and grief.
Loses he both this world and (also) the hereafter; that is a loss (which is) manifest. (Qur’ān, 22:11)
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of accumulating worldly wealth without fear of God?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delivers a profound admonition on the futility of worldly accumulation, noting that whether wealth is acquired through rightful means or withheld from its due, the ultimate outcome is leaving it behind for divine judgment. This sermon underscores the concept of *al-khusran al-mubin* (manifest loss), warning that the anxiety of the grave and the regret of the hereafter stem from mismanaging one's sustenance. The narration serves as a practical guide for believers to evaluate their economic activities not just by legality, but by their spiritual consequence and accountability before Allah.
